written: 2026-11-08, before any out-of-sample result was computed
question: Do simple price-based features predict next-week cross-sectional relative returns of liquid ETFs and of U.S. industry portfolios, out of sample and after trading costs?
reporting_rule: All results are reported whatever they show. Any change to this design after seeing out-of-sample results is logged in design/deviations.md.

etf.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (auto_adjust=False): split-adjusted OHLC, dividend-adjusted close, volume
etf.sample: 2007-04-11 (all 30 trade) to the last complete week
etf.prices: total-return index = dividend-adjusted close; adjusted open = open x (adjusted close / close) of the same day
etf.execution: signal at the close of the last trading day of the week; enter at the next trading day's open; hold until the open after the next signal

french.source: Kenneth French data library: 49 industry portfolios, value-weighted daily returns (CRSP); Fama-French daily RF
french.universe: 49 industries; an industry enters once it has a return
french.prices: total-return index = cumulative product of (1 + daily return)
french.execution: signal at the close of the last trading day of the week; enter at the close of the next trading day (one-day implementation lag); hold until the close of the day after the next signal

etf_only: dvol_surge (log mean dollar volume, 5 days vs 63 days)
features.transform: cross-sectional rank on each signal date, scaled to [-0.5, 0.5]; no time-series scaling

target: holding-period return; models are fitted on its cross-sectional rank scaled to [-0.5, 0.5]

signals.rev_1w: minus the rank of ret_5d (no fitting)
signals.ridge: ridge regression on the ranked features, alpha = 1.0, intercept
signals.lgbm: LightGBM regression: 300 trees, learning_rate 0.02, num_leaves 7, min_data_in_leaf 100, feature_fraction 0.8, bagging_fraction 0.8, bagging_freq 1, lambda_l2 5, seed 0

training.purge: a training week is used only if its holding period ended before the refit signal date

portfolios.long_short: equal-weight long the top 20% and short the bottom 20% by signal (ETF 6 and 6, industries 10 and 10 when all 49 are present); each leg 100% of capital; weights drift between rebalances
portfolios.long_only: equal-weight top 20%, compared with the equal-weight universe

costs.main: 5 bps per unit of traded notional (one-way), plus 50 bps a year borrow on short notional

metrics: weekly rank IC (Spearman of signal vs realized period return)
mean IC, IC information ratio, Newey-West t-stat (4 lags)
long-short annualized return, volatility, Sharpe (52 weeks), max drawdown, annual turnover
Sharpe 95% CI: stationary block bootstrap, mean block 8 weeks, 2000 draws, seed 0
deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) with N = 4 signals per dataset
beta and alpha of long-short returns against the equal-weight universe (Newey-West)
robustness: placebo: training targets permuted across assets within each week; IC should vanish
ETF: enter at the next close instead of the next open
first and second half of the out-of-sample period
decision_rule: A signal counts as working only if, on both datasets, mean OOS IC > 0 with Newey-West t > 2 AND the net-of-cost long-short Sharpe 95% CI excludes 0. Otherwise it is reported as not robust.
